Definition: of Latin origin; feminine of Priscus, ancient; Priska, a Christian woman:--Prisca. See also G4252.
BiblicalUsage: Prisca is Priscilla, the wife of Aquila, and Paul names her three times with honour. He calls her and Aquila his helpers in Christ Jesus, who laid down their own necks for his life, and the churches of the Gentiles thank them. In his last letter he sends her greetings once more, still beside her husband.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Prisca shows what partnership in the gospel looks like: a wife who risks her neck for the apostle and opens her house to the church. I hold her up as proof that the work was never Paul's alone.
